The audit's example: the visible label appears late in the accessible name. This satisfies 2.5.3. Failing it cites the note recommending the label at the start, which W3C classifies as informative, so the finding would be false.
The uncontroversial case: name and label are identical.
A real 2.5.3 failure: the accessible name does not contain the visible text at all, so speech input cannot address the control by the words shown on it.
Undersized, and packed close enough that the 24px circles intersect. No exception applies.
The same undersized target, spaced so the 24px circles do not intersect. The Spacing exception makes it conforming. A reviewer that treats the exceptions as advisory reports this as a defect — the inverse of the A2 failure, and just as wrong.
A link inside a sentence, sized by the line-height around it. The Inline exception applies.
Comfortably over the minimum; nothing to report.
